Duplicate handling works. Refresh **http://maker:4001** and try it:

> **1.** The list already contains "10 Usability Heuristics" (from nngroup.com). Now paste its exact link again — `https://www.nngroup.com/articles/usability-heuristics/` — and press **Save**.
> **2.** Instead of creating a second copy, a message appears: *"You've already saved this link."* — with a **Show it** button.
> **3.** Click **Show it**; the app jumps to and briefly highlights the existing bookmark. (If the existing one happened to be archived, the message says so and takes you to the Archive.)

My reasoning: a duplicate would just clutter the library you're trying to keep findable, so instead of silently adding another, it points you to the one you already have.

Does that match what you'd want when you save something twice — **no duplicate, just take me to the existing one**? Or would you rather it let you save a second copy anyway?
